payload.detail: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-25: turn Railway 'wait for CI' ON, but only once it cannot freeze deploys. Order: (1) fix or remove from the main-push gate the Firefox/WebKit release-browser-matrix failures (#9Z197J), or confirm Railway can wait on pr-required alone; (2) the owner then enables it on the app and worker services. Until then the essential pre-merge checks remain the safeguard. The owner still has to read the actual setting in the Railway dashboard. PRIOR DETAIL: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): Kept at P1 deliberately. Still unverified from the repo (the setting is not in railway.app.json); docs/deployment-architecture.md recorded source.checkSuites false on 2026-09-22 for a preview instance, not production. Counter-argument considered: pr-required already gates merges. But #T82ND3 shows CI on main red after merge on six of eight pushes, which is exactly the case this row covers. Trade-off to weigh: Wait-for-CI makes every deploy wait on the full run and flaky jobs, and pairs with the 2026-09-21 deploy stall. PRIOR DETAIL: Configure a Railway deployment gate on the app and worker services so they wait for pr-required to succeed on the main push. Why: the deploy and the post-merge CI run are two independent reactions to the same push, so 'CI passed' and 'what is live is tested' are different claims. Context: repo maturity review 2026-09-19; inferred from docs/deployment-architecture.md §6 (auto-deploy from main, rollback is a manual redeploy after the fact), NOT from a direct read of Railway settings. Owner: user (Railway dashboard, not code). Confidence: medium — the absence of a gate is inferred from docs; verify in the dashboard first. Depends on: nothing.
